procs.name: Manual Journal Request (MJV)
inbox: A manual journal is needed during month-end close: globally SOP-approved (stock provision, bonus and unutilised-leave accruals) or preventable (corrections / reclasses, manual accruals, Coupa accruals, COBOU, indirect tax)
procs.outdoc: Approved manual journals posted in BlackLine during month-end close; management P&L reviewed
procs.outnote: Hands to R2R-01 SAP Close - journals must be posted before the GL closes at WD+2

steps.d: The Business requestor sends the manual journal request to Embedded Finance. Journal types: globally SOP-approved journals (stock provision, bonus accruals, unutilised leave accruals) and preventable journals (corrections / reclasses, manual accruals, Coupa accruals, COBOU, indirect tax).
steps.src: MJV process flow deck step 1; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.01
steps.rec: Replace the email request with the standard journal request form (MJV-06): mandatory accounting, approval and supporting-document fields, journal type (SOP-approved vs preventable) and reason code (MJV-02). Pre-submission checks (MJV-07, agentic bot with human review) stop incomplete or non-compliant requests before they reach Embedded Finance.
steps.tools: Power Apps form, Power Automate, Copilot Studio agent (pre-submission check), SharePoint request list
steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)
steps.feasc: Register MJV-06 standard journal request form and MJV-07 pre-submission checks: can be implemented in the future (June target flow refers to an agentic bot with human review).

cop.d: A requestor-facing guidance agent grounded on the Global MJV Playbook and the GSOP answers "do I need a manual journal, which type and which supporting documents" before the request is sent, alongside the request form and pre-submission check.

steps.t: Review and approve the cost details
steps.d: Embedded Finance (CFO / FC / CBP) reviews and approves the cost details of the request.
steps.src: MJV process flow deck step 2; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.02
steps.rec: Embedded Finance approval routed from the form by Power Automate with the DOA, and an AI policy / playbook compliance review (MJV-14) surfacing the relevant GSOP requirement and any missing evidence to the approver - the accounting decision stays with Embedded Finance.
steps.tools: Power Automate approval, Copilot Studio (playbook retrieval over the Global MJV Playbook), Email
steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)
steps.feasc: Register MJV-14 AI policy and playbook compliance review - AI-suggested, to be reviewed.

cop.d: Copilot summarises the request thread, checks the cost details against the playbook and drafts the approval or rejection reply for Embedded Finance to review and send.

steps.d: Embedded Finance decides whether a manual journal is required; if not, the request is rejected and the requestor informed.
steps.ex: Cost already captured by an automated accrual - no journal needed
steps.yes: Continue to D2 - GSOP compliance check
steps.no: Reject and inform the requestor - end

steps.d: The GFS Controller checks the journal complies with the Global SOP; non-compliant requests are rejected and the requestor informed. MIRO feedback: no separate compliance review step - the journal is posted directly into BlackLine after manager review.
steps.ex: Accrual request without the supporting calculation required by the GSOP
steps.yes: Continue to step 3 - prepare and post
steps.no: Step 2a - reject and inform the requestor
steps.src: MJV process flow deck decision 2.2; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.03

fix.d: The GFS Controller rejects the non-compliant request and informs the requestor (deck: end).
pp: Lack of consistent accounting interpretation and governance across markets
fix.rec: Rejection and the reason code returned to the requestor automatically from the form (MJV-02 reason codes), so rejected and deferred requests are counted in the dashboard rather than lost in email.
fix.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)
fix.feasc: Register MJV-02 standardised header text and reason codes: can be implemented in the future.

cop.d: Copilot drafts the rejection note to the requestor with the GSOP reason and the playbook reference, for the approver to review before sending.

steps.d: The GFS Controller prepares the journal and posts it in BlackLine (to SAP).
steps.src: MJV process flow deck step 3; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.04
out: Journal posted before the GL close
pp: Heavy reliance on manual journals (MJV) and human intervention during close activities
Errors, inconsistencies and audit scrutiny risks arising from manual corrections
Competing priorities between manual close activities and automation initiatives
steps.rec: Deterministic journal validation before the BlackLine load (MJV-12: required fields, balanced debits and credits, duplicate references, valid GL and cost-centre combinations, approvals and evidence), AI anomaly and duplicate detection (MJV-15), a structured root-cause category captured in the BlackLine comments (MJV-04) with AI-assisted classification (MJV-13), and an AI-drafted, source-cited journal explanation for the preparer to edit (MJV-17).
steps.tools: Python validation service, BlackLine journal template and comments, Copilot Studio (classification and explanation draft), SAP
steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)
steps.feasc: Register MJV-12 / 13 / 15 / 17: AI-suggested, to be reviewed; MJV-04 root cause in BlackLine comments: can be implemented in the future.

cop.d: An agent proposes the journal classification and drafts the explanation text for the BlackLine comment from the request and the supporting documents; the GFS Controller reviews and posts.

steps.d: The GFS Manager reviews and approves the journal; it is posted directly into BlackLine after manager review (MIRO feedback: no compliance review step after this).
steps.src: MJV process flow deck step 4; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.05; MIRO feedback 5
steps.rec: The GFS Manager approves in BlackLine with the validation result, anomaly and duplicate flags (MJV-15) and the playbook check summary attached to the journal, so review time goes to the exceptions.
steps.tools: BlackLine approval workflow, Python / Copilot Studio outputs attached as journal support
steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)
steps.feasc: Register MJV-15 AI anomaly and duplicate journal detection - AI-suggested, to be reviewed.

steps.d: GFS FP&A reviews the management P&L after the journals are posted.
steps.src: MJV process flow deck step 5; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.06
steps.rec: GFS FP&A reviews the management P&L with the APAC manual journal dashboard (MJV-01) showing posted journals by account, market and root cause; the BlackLine extract and Power BI refresh are scheduled (MJV-11) so the view is current at the time of review.
steps.tools: Power BI (APAC MJV dashboard), scheduled BlackLine export / API, Python cleansing
steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)
steps.feasc: Under review: marked for review in Lai Leng Ng's feedback on the updated E2E for Controlling (16 Oct 2026). Register MJV-01 APAC manual journal dashboard and MJV-11 scheduled extraction and refresh are the items it builds on.

cop.d: Copilot summarises the manual journals posted in the period by account, market and root cause from the dashboard, so the reviewer starts from the exceptions.

steps.d: If the management P&L review finds an issue, the GFS Controller corrects the journal and it goes back through prepare, post and approval (deck: back to step 3); otherwise the journal stands.
steps.ex: Accrual posted to the wrong cost centre
steps.no: Step 6 - correct the journal, then back to prepare and post (step 3)

fix.d: The GFS Controller corrects the journal; it goes back to prepare and post (step 3) and through the manager approval again.
fix.src: MJV process flow deck step 6; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.07
pp: Errors, inconsistencies and audit scrutiny risks arising from manual corrections
Focus on downstream symptom correction rather than upstream root-cause prevention
High volume of rework and correction journals impacting productivity
fix.rec: Each correction journal carries its root-cause category (MJV-04); recurring-pattern insights (MJV-16) cluster repeat corrections by cause, requestor, market and account and propose the upstream fix, which is assigned to an accountable owner with a due date (MJV-05) instead of being corrected again next close.
fix.tools: BlackLine comments, Python / Copilot Studio clustering, Power Apps remediation tracker, Power BI
fix.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)
fix.feasc: Register MJV-04 and MJV-05: can be implemented in the future; MJV-16 recurring-pattern insights: AI-suggested, to be reviewed.

cop.d: An agent groups the correction reasons raised in BlackLine comments and suggests the likely root cause and the playbook rule, to feed the preventable-journal loop.

opp.d: Dashboard (MJV-01) identifies the highest-volume requestors and causes (MJV-08); each preventable cause gets an accountable upstream owner and due date (MJV-05); benefits and recurrence are tracked automatically (MJV-21) and reviewed with CFOs monthly and AA leadership quarterly (MJV-09) - the mechanism behind the 30 percent MJV reduction target.
opp.feasc: Register MJV-05 / 08 / 09: can be implemented in the future; MJV-21 automated benefit and recurrence tracking: AI-suggested, to be reviewed.

opp.t: Governed journal pipeline: request form → validation → BlackLine → dashboard, scaled across towers
opp.d: One intake form, one validation service, root cause captured at posting and one governed journal dataset published for every team posting through BlackLine (MJV-10), with natural-language Q&A over the journal history for authorised users (MJV-18).
opp.feasc: Register MJV-10 scale the dashboard across towers: can be implemented in the future; MJV-18: AI-suggested, to be reviewed.

procs.name: Statutory audit end-to-end (seven sub-processes)
procs.owner: Controlling with Embedded Finance, Tax, all towers and the auditors
inbox: Annual statutory audit cycle: audit scope and timeline agreed with the auditors
procs.outdoc: Audited and filed statutory financial statements; P13 audit adjustments posted and retained earnings reconciled
procs.outnote: Post-audit review and CI, and compliance & controls management are named in the MIRO feedback but not documented

steps.d: Conduct the planning meeting with the auditors, Embedded Finance, Tax and the GFS teams; align scope, timeline, walkthroughs and the audit approach.
steps.src: Controlling key processes workbook · Audit Planning & Kick-off; process register (all towers), row CTRL-02.01
pp: Late stakeholder alignment, incomplete planning information
steps.ci: Centralised KPMG planning model; 'test once, use often' (TPI 2026)
steps.rec: Planning starts from the centralised KPMG planning model (TPI 2026) plus an early audit-risk signal workflow (AUD-08): potential statutory issues and adjustments logged with owner, entity, impact, evidence and due date during the year, and predictive escalation alerts (AUD-20) on ageing and workload before the timetable slips.
steps.tools: Power Apps audit-risk log, Power Automate alerts, Power BI, KPMG Clara / KCC
steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)
steps.feasc: Register AUD-08 early audit-risk signal workflow: can be implemented in the future (Controlling plans an audit adjustment dashboard to identify recurring issues before the next cycle); AUD-20: AI-suggested, to be reviewed.

steps.d: Support the auditor walkthroughs and explain the key finance processes and controls across the process towers.
steps.src: Controlling key processes workbook · Process Walkthrough & Risk Assessment; process register (all towers), row CTRL-02.02
pp: Multiple process tower coordination
steps.rec: Walkthrough narratives kept in the centralised repository (TPI 2026, 'test once, use often') and drafted for update each year from the documented SOPs and these Demand to Profit process maps by a Copilot agent, so towers confirm changes rather than rewrite the walkthrough.
steps.tools: SharePoint walkthrough repository, Copilot Studio over the SOP library and process maps
steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)

cop.d: An agent grounded on the SOP library and the process maps answers walkthrough questions and drafts the risk-assessment notes for the control owner to confirm.

steps.d: Coordinate the collection and submission of audit evidence (PBCs) from the process towers and local teams into the KPMG Clara / KCC repository.
steps.src: Controlling key processes workbook · Audit PBC Preparation & Submission; process register (all towers), row CTRL-02.03
pp: High manual effort, duplicate requests, incorrect request routing
steps.ci: KPMG Clara / KCC central repository; direct process-owner routing and owner matrix (TPI 2026)
steps.rec: PBC requests follow the cross-tower taxonomy (AUD-01, standard PBC in KCC) and route directly to the tower owner from the owner matrix (AUD-02, AUD-14); evidence is produced in batches - SAP listings by scheduled job or a KCC t-code for the KPMG central team (AUD-03), bulk Coupa invoice retrieval (AUD-04, TDT tool) - and matched sample-to-evidence before submission (AUD-18). Governed evidence packages (AUD-05) are kept in view for year two.
steps.tools: KPMG Clara / KCC, SAP scheduled jobs, Coupa bulk retrieval (TDT tool), Python manifest and matching, SharePoint
steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)
steps.feasc: Register AUD-01 / 02 already implemented (KCC); AUD-03 / 04 / 14 feasible; AUD-18 AI-suggested, to be reviewed; AUD-05 can be implemented in the future (KIV in year one).

cop.tool: AI Builder document processing / Azure AI Document Intelligence
cop.d: Evidence documents are read automatically and matched to the PBC request list, so missing or mismatched items are flagged before the pack is submitted.

steps.d: Coordinate the responses to audit samples, information requests and follow-up queries across the towers.
steps.src: Controlling key processes workbook · Audit Fieldwork & Query Management; process register (all towers), row CTRL-02.04
pp: Large sample sizes, multi-tower dependencies, repeated follow-ups
steps.ci: Centralised audit testing performed by KL and Group teams (TPI 2026)
steps.rec: One consolidated register for original and follow-up KPMG questions with inter-office confirmation for eligible intercompany balances (AUD-09, with the KPMG UK intercompany DA), semantic duplicate-request detection against open and completed KCC items (AUD-15), AI-drafted responses grounded only in approved evidence for the owner to finalise (AUD-17), and the cross-tower governance view from KCC (AUD-07).
steps.tools: KPMG Clara / KCC status data, Power BI, Copilot Studio (duplicate detection and response drafts), Power Apps query register
steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)
steps.feasc: Register AUD-09 feasible (needs Hammond / Simon alignment); AUD-07 already implemented via the KCC site; AUD-15 / 17 AI-suggested, to be reviewed.

cop.d: An agent finds duplicate auditor queries and drafts responses from earlier answers and the stored evidence, for the process owner to review.

steps.d: Review the financial statements, disclosures and audit comments with Embedded Finance and the auditors; the statutory financial statements are prepared by SG Deloitte and reviewed in Wdesk / Workiva.
steps.src: Controlling key processes workbook · Financial Statement Review; process register (all towers), row CTRL-02.05
pp: Multiple review rounds and version control
Inconsistent use of Wdesk / Workiva and late access - queries raised by email and re-keyed into Wdesk
Quality issues in the FS prepared by SG Deloitte (disclosures, casting, cross-references, balance presentation)
steps.ci: Keep to a 3x FS revision approach, tracked and monitored (TPI 2026)
steps.rec: Financial statement review run end-to-end in Wdesk / Workiva with the 3x revision approach tracked (TPI 2026): queries raised in Wdesk rather than by email, and an automated pre-review of each draft from SG Deloitte - casting, cross-references, disclosure checklist, balance presentation against the trial balance - so Controlling's rounds focus on judgement, not arithmetic.
steps.tools: Wdesk / Workiva, Python checks on the FS extract vs trial balance, disclosure checklist in SharePoint
steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)

cop.d: Copilot compares the financial statement extract with the disclosure checklist and the prior year text and lists the differences for the reviewer.

steps.rec: P13 adjustments tracked on standardised templates (TPI 2026) with AI root-cause clustering of adjustments and findings by process, account, entity and cause (AUD-19) feeding the audit adjustment dashboard (AUD-08) and the MJV prevention backlog, so recurring audit issues are fixed before the next cycle.
steps.tools: Power Apps adjustment tracker, Copilot Studio / Python clustering, Power BI, SAP (P13), BlackLine
steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)
steps.feasc: Register AUD-19 AI audit-adjustment root-cause clustering - AI-suggested, to be reviewed; links to the audit adjustment dashboard Controlling plans (AUD-08 remark).

cop.d: An agent clusters the audit adjustments by cause and drafts the P13 posting note for the preparer to review.

steps.opp: Claude recommendation from the As-Is map (Controlling workbook, MJV deck, register - Oct 2026)
